title: Compact admissible balls and bound-preserving one-vector extension
statement: Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field] with a multiplicative absolute value $|\cdot|:K\to\mathbf R_{\geq0}$, meaning $|a|=0$ exactly when $a=0$, $|1|=1$, and $|ab|=|a||b|$. Assume $|a+b|\leq\max(|a|,|b|)$, and assume every closed ball $\{b\in K:|b-c|\leq r\}$, for $c\in K$ and $r\geq0$, is compact for $d(a,b)=|a-b|$. Let $V$ be a $K$-vector space with a norm $\|\cdot\|:V\to\mathbf R_{\geq0}$ satisfying $\|v\|=0$ exactly when $v=0$, $\|av\|=|a|\|v\|$, and $\|v+w\|\leq\max(\|v\|,\|w\|)$. Let $U\subseteq V$ be any linear subspace, $C>0$ a real number, $g:U\to K$ a $K$-linear map with $|g(u)|\leq C\|u\|$ for every $u\in U$, and $x\in V\setminus U$. For $u\in U$ put $R_u=C\|x-u\|$ and $B_u=\{b\in K:|b-g(u)|\leq R_u\}$. Each $B_u$ is nonempty and closed, and $R_u\leq R_v$ implies $B_u\subseteq B_v$. For every finite $F\subseteq U$, the set $B_0\cap\bigcap_{u\in F}B_u$ is nonempty, including $F=\varnothing$, and $\bigcap_{u\in U}B_u\ne\varnothing$. For every $b$ in this last intersection, the formula $G(u+ax)=g(u)+ab$ ($u\in U$, $a\in K$) defines a $K$-linear map $G:U+Kx\to K$, where $Kx=\{ax:a\in K\}$ and $U+Kx=\{u+ax:u\in U,\ a\in K\}$. It restricts to $g$ and satisfies $|G(y)|\leq C\|y\|$ for every $y\in U+Kx$. No closedness or completeness of $U$ or $V$, and no nontriviality of the scalar absolute value, is required. Linearity means additivity and preservation of scalar multiplication.

proof.text: From [def-weil-field], $(-1)^2=1$; multiplicativity and nonnegativity give $|-1|=1$, so $|-a|=|a|$ and $\|-v\|=\|v\|$. The ultrametric inequality implies the ordinary triangle inequality. Each radius $R_u$ is nonnegative, and $g(u)\in B_u$. To check closedness, if $z\notin B_u$, put $\epsilon=|z-g(u)|-R_u>0$. Whenever $|w-z|<\epsilon$, the triangle inequality gives $|w-g(u)|\geq |z-g(u)|-|w-z|>R_u$. Thus the complement is open.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent scalar-extension expansion: nonempty closed admissible balls; direct metric calculation

proof.text:
For $u,v\in U$, linearity and the bound on $g$ give
$$|g(u)-g(v)|\leq C\|u-v\|\leq C\max(\|x-u\|,\|x-v\|)=\max(R_u,R_v).$$
If $R_u\leq R_v$ and $b\in B_u$, then
$$|b-g(v)|\leq\max(|b-g(u)|,|g(u)-g(v)|)\leq R_v.$$
Therefore $B_u\subseteq B_v$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent scalar-extension expansion: ultrametric nesting calculation

proof.text: For finite $F\subseteq U$, the finite nonempty set $F\cup\{0\}$ has an index $u_*$ of least radius. The preceding inclusion gives $B_{u_*}\subseteq B_0\cap\bigcap_{u\in F}B_u$, so $g(u_*)$ lies in that intersection. This includes $F=\varnothing$: choose $u_*=0$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent scalar-extension expansion: finite intersections, including the empty family

proof.text: Give $B_0$ its subspace topology and put $C_u=B_0\cap B_u$, viewed as a subset of $B_0$. The compact-ball hypothesis says every open cover of this subspace has a finite subcover. Each $C_u$ is closed there: its complement is the intersection of $B_0$ with the open complement of $B_u$. Step 3 gives every finite intersection of the $C_u$, including the empty intersection $B_0$, a point. Apply [lem-sfb-compact-closed-finite-intersection] with $X=B_0$ and $I=U$. Its conclusion is a point of $B_0\cap\bigcap_{u\in U}B_u$, hence of $\bigcap_{u\in U}B_u$.

source.place: Tag 005D, lemma-intersection-closed-in-quasi-compact; applied to the compact subspace B_0

proof.text: Fix any $b\in\bigcap_{u\in U}B_u$. Every element of $U+Kx$ has a unique expression $u+ax$: if $u+ax=v+cx$ and $a\ne c$, the inverse supplied by [def-weil-field] gives $x=(a-c)^{-1}(v-u)\in U$, a contradiction; thus $a=c$ and $u=v$. Hence $G(u+ax)=g(u)+ab$ is well-defined. Addition of pairs $(u,a)$ and scalar multiplication of pairs give, respectively, $G(y+z)=G(y)+G(z)$ and $G(ty)=tG(y)$ by linearity of $g$ and distributivity. The pair $(u,0)$ gives $G(u)=g(u)$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent scalar-extension expansion: uniqueness of coordinates and explicit linear extension

proof.text:
For $y=u+ax$, if $a=0$ the required bound is that of $g$. If $a\ne0$, put $v=-a^{-1}u\in U$, using [def-weil-field]. Then $y=a(x-v)$ and $g(u)=-ag(v)$, so admissibility of $b$ gives
$$|G(y)|=|a|\,|b-g(v)|\leq |a|C\|x-v\|=C\|y\|.$$
This holds for every admissible $b$. The proof uses neither a scalar of absolute value strictly between zero and one nor any closedness or completeness of $U$ or $V$.

Steps 1–3 and 5–6 are elementary from def-weil-field and the hypotheses, and I checked each one. |−1|=1 gives the symmetry. ‖u−v‖≤max(‖x−u‖,‖x−v‖) gives |g(u)−g(v)|≤max(R_u,R_v), so the balls nest the right way. The least radius on F∪{0} handles F=∅. The coordinates are unique because x=(a−c)^{-1}(v−u) would lie in U. With v=−a^{-1}u we get y=a(x−v) and G(y)=a(b−g(v)), so |G(y)|≤C‖y‖ with the same C. The statement is self-contained and matches what the parent lem-sfb-proper-ultrametric-scalar-extension step 2 uses, which is exactly the local extension condition of lem-sfb-bounded-extension-zorn. It does not restate a clause of the parent. Blueprint main-20261015 direct-images paragraph (3) has no such argument, and proof_origin=agent is honest about that.
